title: How do home-service companies stop missing customer enquiries?
description: Home-service companies stop missing customer enquiries by capturing every call and message in one place, collecting the job details the first time, and tracking each enquiry until it has a booked visit or a quote request with the estimator.

summary.question: How do home-service companies stop missing customer enquiries?
summary.answer: Home-service companies stop missing customer enquiries by capturing every call and message in one place, collecting the job details the first time, and tracking each enquiry until it has a booked visit or a quote request with the estimator. Enquiries are most often missed while the crew is on a job and nobody is free to answer, take details or call back.
takeaways: Capture every enquiry in one place, including calls that came in while the team was busy.
Collect the trade, address, problem and preferred timing in the first contact.
Check the service area and the schedule before proposing a visit.
Track each enquiry until it has a booked visit or a quote request.
Escalate urgent safety issues straight away under your emergency procedure.

scope.covers: Plumbing, HVAC, electrical and roofing enquiries: where they get missed, what details to collect, and how to move each one to a booked visit or quote request.
scope.excludes: Diagnosis, safety advice, repair instructions, binding quotes, discounts, dispatch commitments and live emergency response.
scope.instead: Those go to your dispatcher, estimator or duty contact. Urgent issues follow your business emergency procedure.

sections.heading: Why do enquiries get missed?
paragraphs: Most home-service teams are busy and on the move. The people who could answer the phone are often on a roof, under a sink or driving between jobs.
list: Calls go to voicemail and are not returned the same day.
Details are taken on scraps of paper, so the estimator has to call the customer again.
Enquiries from outside the service area take up time before anyone checks.
A proposed visit time is mistaken for a confirmed one.
Quote requests wait because nobody owns them.

sections.heading: How do you stop it?
list: Capture every call, message and web form in one shared list, with the time it came in.
Collect the trade, address, problem and preferred timing the first time, so nobody has to ask again.
Check the service area and the schedule before proposing a visit.
Pass quote requests to the estimator with everything they need to price the job.
Keep the enquiry open until a visit is booked, the quote request is with the estimator, or the customer says no.

sections.heading: What should stay with people?
paragraphs: Diagnosis, safety decisions, repair instructions, binding quotes, discounts and dispatch commitments need qualified or authorised staff. Never give a price that has not been approved.
Urgent issues, such as a burning smell near an electrical panel, follow your emergency procedure straight away. They should never wait in a queue.

sections.heading: How do you know it is working?
paragraphs: Count the enquiries that reach a confirmed next step, and track missed enquiries, the time to book a visit or hand over a quote request, and dispatcher effort. Record these before you change anything, so you have something to compare with.

faq.q: Why do home-service companies miss enquiries?
faq.a: Because the people who could answer are usually out on jobs. Calls go to voicemail, details get lost, and call-backs slip to the next day.

faq.q: What details should we collect from a new enquiry?
faq.a: The trade, the address, the problem in the customer’s own words and the preferred timing. With those, the dispatcher or estimator can act without calling back.

faq.q: Can an automatic reply quote a price?
faq.a: Not a binding one. Only approved pricing can be shared, and complex jobs, inspections and price exceptions go to your estimator.
Escalate them at once under your emergency procedure. An urgent safety issue should never wait in an enquiry queue.
